_meta.beschreibung: Case-study data of the Promptotyping methodology site. The sources are the case descriptions in the vault, the method extensions in the Promptotyping MOC and the case analysis in Pollin 2026, Section 4. The gallery groups by the role a case plays for the paper and orders within a block by the five epistemic interface functions, the site's own typology documented on the artefact page (part 4 of the specification).
_meta.kuratierung: Admission is decided by what a card lets a reader check. Every case in Table 3 of the paper (Section 4.3) has a card, because a reader who comes from the case analysis to verify a claim has to find the project; the paper_row field carries that link and tools/check_consistency.py holds it in both directions (operator decision 2026-07-26, re-keyed to the five-chapter text with the promotion of 2026-07-30). Beyond the paper's case set the gallery carries the projects the method grew out of, the teaching formats, and the documented applications that the earlier seven-chapter text listed in its project inventory; since the promotion those stand on their repositories alone under the role further. The Aldersbach monastic accounts stay although the paper dropped the case as too old, because the genealogy is what they carry (operator decision 2026-07-25). Outside the gallery stays the agentic edition pipeline, which is meta-tooling and a template rather than a single research artefact.

schema.id: anchor slug, forming the site anchor together with #case- (e.g. herdata -> #case-herdata)
schema.name: display name
schema.role: what the case argues for, one of evidence, genealogy, teaching, further; the gallery breaks on this at the top level and orders within a block by interfaceTypes. Labels in role_labels, one-line notes in role_notes
schema.interfaceTypes: array of verification, exploration, edition, capture, audit, the five epistemic functions of the site's interface typology (artefact page, part 4 of the specification); empty where the case produced no interface. This is the gallery's ordering and filtering dimension since 2026-07-26, replacing a nine-value vocabulary of the site's own. The promoted paper's Table 2 names five artefact forms of its own; whether the site typology follows it is an open operator decision (2026-07-30)
schema.insight: methodological contribution as recorded at curation; the paper's own per-case findings stand in Table 3 (Section 4.3), otherwise null
schema.deep_page: true where the case carries a depth page under _content/case-studies/
schema.paper_row: exact case name in Table 3 of the paper (Section 4.3), or null where the project is outside the paper's case set; checked by tools/check_consistency.py against knowledge/paper.md

role_notes.evidence: Carries a row of the cross-case findings in Pollin 2026, Table 3 (Section 4.3). A claim of that analysis can be checked against these.
role_notes.genealogy: Built before the method had its vocabulary. The opening of Section 2 reads them as the ground it grew from.
role_notes.teaching: Recorded sessions and teaching builds. The teachability argument at the end of Section 4.3 rests on this kind of material.
role_notes.further: Documented applications the paper does not carry. They stand on their repositories alone.

caseStudies.name: teiCrafter
caseStudies.summary: Idea of 2023, a Custom GPT that converted plain text to TEI-XML (P5) from a mapping rule under editor-in-the-loop control, with no software written for it; the same idea was taken up in 2026 and built as a browser-based lossless TEI editor once the agentic tooling carried it.
caseStudies.data: Plain text and transcriptions in 2023, arbitrary TEI-XML in the editor since 2026
caseStudies.artifact: Custom GPT without implemented software (2023), browser-based lossless TEI editor (2026)
caseStudies.insight: Origin point of the method as a prompt-configured idea; what separates 2023 from 2026 is the maturity of the coding tooling that made the same idea buildable

caseStudies.name: Stefan Zweig Digital Annotation Tool
caseStudies.summary: First publicly documented Promptotyping experiment, a timeline-based annotation tool for correspondence data from Stefan Zweig Digital, built in about two hours.
caseStudies.data: XML correspondence metadata from Stefan Zweig Digital
caseStudies.artifact: Timeline annotation tool as a single page application
caseStudies.insight: Critical Expert in the Loop (two-hour experiment, first blog post)

caseStudies.artifact: HTR/OCR pipeline with facsimile-text viewer and statistics dashboard
caseStudies.insight: Introduced in Section 2.3; the record's production-scale pipeline

caseStudies.name: Knowledge and Project Management with Obsidian

caseStudies.artifact: A vault that holds the rules by which it grows

caseStudies.name: Knowledge Organisation across Three Tools

caseStudies.data: A video on generative-AI fundamentals as source material
caseStudies.artifact: Knowledge document, vault entry and an infographic
caseStudies.insight: Tool differentiation across chat, agentic environment and image generation, with the human holding the workflow together
